segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin frequently call this their favorite cleanser, describing softer, more hydrated skin with no post-wash tightness, though one reviewer whose skin gets drier in winter found it insanely drying and switched cleansers after five nights.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin (oily zones with drier patches) generally report it balances both areas without stripping, but a couple with more oil-prone combination skin found it left an oily film or didn't remove enough oil before bed.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers, including some with reactive or temperamental skin, repeatedly describe it as non-irritating and gentle, with several calling it a holy-grail product; one sensitive-skin reviewer instead reacted badly to the scent.
segments.mature: Several reviewers in their 40s and 50s with dry or aging skin describe it as a long-time holy-grail cleanser that keeps their skin hydrated and smooth.

concerns.dehydration: Dry-skin reviewers overwhelmingly report the cleanser leaves their face soft, hydrated and free of tightness, including some with 'extremely dry' or long-term aging skin who call it their holy grail; one reviewer with winter-dry skin instead found it insanely drying and switched products after several uses.
concerns.blemishes: Many reviewers, including some who are acne- or hormonal-acne-prone, report fewer breakouts or that the cleanser doesn't clog pores; a smaller number describe new pimples, blackheads or increased oiliness after starting it.
concerns.oiliness: Several reviewers, mostly with oily or combination-oily skin, say the cream doesn't lather enough to fully clear oil and can leave a residue or oily film, especially at night after wearing makeup or sunscreen; others report it leaves skin soft without excess oil.

Doesn't fully remove makeup or sunscreen alone
A little product goes a long way
Clean ingredient list valued by buyers

extraits.titre: I got breakouts due to this cleanser
extraits.texte: I wanted to like this cleanser so bad but I have been using it for a week now and started noticing pimples popping up out of no where. I know this from the cleanser because its the only new product I started using on my face. Also the scent is horrendous and my face feels oily all day after using it :(

I was looking for a cream cleanser for wintertime, because my skin tends to get much more dry in the colder months. Decided to try this one and it was a waste of money. While it did remove regular makeup ok, it does not remove sunscreen or waterproof makeup well at all. Moreover, it was insanely drying for my skin…as soon as I rinsed it, my face felt like it was wrinkling up like a raisin! I thought I might just be battling an extra dry phase, so I continued to use it the next few nights only to find my skin becoming more and more dry. After 5 nights, my face was insanely dry, parched, and rough. I switched to LaRoche Posay Toleraine gentle cleanser, and after 2 nights, my skin began to normalize again thank goodness! If you have very oily skin that is NOT prone to dry patches or dehydration, this one from Mad Hippie may work for you…otherwise, if you're prone to any facial dryness or dehydration, stay far away from this one.

It doesn't clean well enough and leaves behind an oily film. It's obvious, the first time I used it I knew it was one of *those* cleansers that doesn't actually cleanse. I appreciate that it's not stripping but I could not use this by itself I have to add my regular cleanser into this. It's very nice in conjunction with another harsher soap so I kept it. I use the kombucha andalou naturals typically & it's a little bit too stripping sometimes so a dab of both work pretty perfectly for me. It's not a terrible product it's just too oily. I actually would buy it again to use as a buffer in cleansing.

extraits.titre: Amazing Product! Iffy On the Packaging
extraits.texte: This is my favorite Mad Hippie product and I can 100% see myself repurchasing this. I have combination skin that is oily around my nose and upper eyelid but dry everywhere else so a lot of cleansers can be quite stripping. I actually don't like products that get too foamy/bubbly for that reason. This is the most gentle and nourishing cleanser I have ever used. It moisturizes as it cleanses, doesn't foam up so you know there are no harsh surfactants. I you have very oily or acne prone skin this might not be your jam to really deep clean. I mostly use this as a morning cleanser because my skin is not that dirty in the morning but it's just enough to be refreshing, wash off the nighttime skincare products, and remove a bit of oil on my nose that builds up overnight. At night I found it also works as the first step in a double cleanse because it is oil-based so it can very gently breakdown my waterproof mascara and SPF. I usually use a different product for 2nd step at night to cleanse a bit deeper. Scent wise, it is a very subtle florally scent from the orchid extract. It is very non-irritating. Thankfully there is no citrus like most other MH products. Sensitive skin friendly!

In my 41 years, I must have gone through about a dozen cleansers that claim to be non-drying and none of them worked until I stumbled upon Mad Hippie's cream cleanser. It is the holy grail of cream cleansers and keeps my dry, aging skin hydrated. I think I might finally be a product monogamist.

love, love, LOVE this product. its so clean, creamy and leaves my skin so hydrated and this cleanser doesnt strip the skin. i have dry, sensitive, acne prone skin and this product works wonders for me. i wish that it did come in a bigger bottle, i use twice a day and this lasts me abt a month. not a fan of the pump like other reviews are saying it is a bit annoying but would recommend this brand to anyone with a similar skin type + likes clean natural ingredients for a great price!
